plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 4: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.

interactionPlan.concept: A logistic curve accelerates until the population reaches half the carrying capacity (the inflection point), then decelerates as it asymptotically approaches the ceiling y = c; the parameter b controls how abruptly that transition occurs.
elements: horizontal axis labeled t, double-arrowed, no numeric ticks
vertical axis labeled f(t), double-arrowed, no numeric ticks
dashed orange horizontal line y = c with left-end label 'y = c'
black leader line from the dashed line to the annotation 'Carrying capacity'
solid dark-blue logistic curve f(t) = c/(1 + a e^{-bx}) entering from lower left, crossing the vertical axis, steepening, then flattening just below y = c
filled dot at (0, c/(1+a)) with leader to annotation 'Initial value of population'
filled dot at (ln(a)/b, c/2) with leader to annotation 'Point of maximum growth'
blue formula label 'f(t) = c/(1 + a e^{-bx})' placed right of the upper bend
moving marker dot on the curve driven by the time slider
tangent line segment at the moving marker showing instantaneous slope
live readout showing f(t), the tangent slope, and the gap c - f(t)

interactions.label: Time t
interactions.teaches: Sweeping t moves a marker along the curve while the tangent slope and the gap to y = c update together: the slope is largest exactly at f(t) = c/2 and shrinks toward zero as the curve saturates, so growth is fastest at half the carrying capacity and then slows

interactions.label: Growth rate b
interactions.teaches: Increasing b makes the S-curve steeper and pulls the maximum-growth point leftward (ln(a)/b decreases), showing that b sets both the timing and the intensity of the transition from accelerating to saturating growth

demo_steps.title: Read the three landmarks
demo_steps.narration: The curve starts at the initial value c/(1+a) on the vertical axis, climbs steepest at the inflection point (ln(a)/b, c/2), and levels off toward the dashed carrying-capacity line y = c without ever touching it.

demo_steps.title: Sweep time to feel the slope
demo_steps.narration: Drag the time slider: the tangent is steepest when the marker sits at c/2, then flattens as the gap c - f(t) closes, making visible that the growth rate peaks at half capacity and then decays.

demo_steps.title: Change the growth rate b
demo_steps.narration: Raise or lower b and watch the whole S-curve steepen or flatten while the maximum-growth dot slides horizontally, showing that b controls how abruptly the population makes its transition toward saturation.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Logistic growth is fastest precisely when the population equals half the carrying capacity; before that the rate rises, after that it falls toward zero as the curve saturates, and b governs how sharp that turning point is.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use unscaled double-arrowed axes (t horizontal, f(t) vertical) with no tick numbers, matching the sketch. Draw the carrying capacity as a dashed orange horizontal line near the top with 'y = c' at its left and a 'Carrying capacity' leader annotation. Plot the logistic curve in solid dark blue using internal constants c = 100, a = 9 (so initial value = 10 and inflection at t = ln(9)/b, value 50); print the formula f(t) = c/(1 + a e^{-bx}) in blue to the right of the upper bend. Mark the two key points with filled dots and black leader lines to 'Initial value of population' and 'Point of maximum growth'. The time-slider marker and its tangent segment should be a contrasting color (e.g., magenta/red) with a small live readout of f(t), slope, and c - f(t); recompute the tangent and the inflection dot whenever b changes so the two sliders stay coupled.
